name: Gray leaf spot
advice: Rotate away from maize, plough under infected residue and grow tolerant hybrids; avoid very dense planting so leaves dry faster.

name: Common rust
advice: Usually minor on field maize: grow resistant hybrids and sow on time so the crop escapes peak rust weather.

name: Northern leaf blight
advice: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops and bury infected residue after harvest.

name: Healthy
advice: No disease detected. Keep scouting the crop weekly, especially after warm, humid spells.

name: Bacterial spot
advice: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants, avoid overhead watering and remove badly infected leaves.

name: Early blight
advice: Remove infected lower leaves, mulch so soil does not splash onto leaves, and rotate away from tomato and potato for 2-3 years.

name: Late blight
advice: Spreads fast in cool, wet weather: remove and destroy infected plants promptly and keep foliage dry.

name: Leaf mold
advice: Mostly a problem in humid, enclosed conditions: improve ventilation, space plants wider and avoid wetting leaves.

name: Septoria leaf spot
advice: Remove infected lower leaves, mulch, avoid overhead irrigation and rotate crops.

name: Spider mites
advice: A pest, not a disease, favoured by hot, dry, dusty conditions: spray leaves with water to dislodge mites and protect natural predators.

name: Target spot
advice: Improve airflow, remove infected leaves and crop debris, and avoid long periods of leaf wetness.

name: Yellow leaf curl virus
advice: Spread by whiteflies and cannot be cured: remove infected plants, control whiteflies with yellow sticky traps and insect-proof nursery nets, and grow resistant varieties.

name: Mosaic virus
advice: Spread by contact and on tools: remove infected plants, wash hands and disinfect tools, and grow resistant varieties.

name: Healthy
advice: No disease detected. Keep scouting the crop weekly.
